content.text:
I fixed the legacy-namespace bug, but I couldn't run the unit tests, so the change is unverified.

**The fix.** `SyndHandler.startPrefixMapping` only registered the iTunes handler for the lowercase URI `http://www.itunes.com/dtds/podcast-1.0.dtd`. A feed declaring `http://www.itunes.com/DTDs/Podcast-1.0.dtd`, like the MBC feed, was never recognised. Its `<itunes:image>` and other iTunes-only metadata were dropped. I added the mixed-case URI as `Itunes.NSURI2` and accepted either URI in `SyndHandler.java`. The change follows how `PodcastIndex` handles its two URIs. Nothing else changes for feeds that use the lowercase URI.

**Test.** I added `testItunesLegacyNamespace` to `RssParserTest`. It parses the new fixture `feed-rss-testItunesLegacyNamespace.xml`, which has the mixed-case namespace and an `<itunes:image>` but no `<image>`. It asserts `feed.getImageUrl()` is the iTunes image. I didn't write it first to show the failure before the fix.

**Tests not run.** `./gradlew --offline :parser:feed:test` fails at configuration with "Plugin com.android.application 9.0.1 was not found". The Gradle user home has no cached dependencies. The read-only dependency cache that `GRADLE_RO_DEP_CACHE` points to, `C:\abb\caches\gradle-ro\antennapod`, gives "Access denied" in this environment. I didn't try to get around that access restriction. Please run `./gradlew --offline --console=plain :parser:feed:test` where the cache is readable.
